name: Belmond Palacio Nazarenas
insider_take: This isn't just a luxury hotel—it's a 500-year-old former convent and palace where Inca stones meet colonial grandeur in the heart of the ancient Inca capital.
whats_special: Built on original Inca foundations with walls dating back to the 15th century, this architectural marvel features Peru's first outdoor heated pool and an on-site oxygen-enriched spa to combat Cusco's 11,200-foot altitude. The property showcases priceless colonial art and artifacts, while each suite boasts underfloor heating and individually controlled oxygen systems.
pro_tip: Arrive a day early to acclimatize at the hotel's oxygen-enriched spa before exploring Machu Picchu—the concierge can arrange exclusive dawn access via the luxury Hiram Bingham train.
dont_miss: The hotel's private entrance to the adjacent San Antonio Abad Seminary, evening pisco tastings in the historic courtyard, and the rooftop terrace views of Cusco's red-tiled roofs with the Andes as your backdrop. The hotel is just steps from Qorikancha, the golden Inca temple that once held the empire's most sacred ceremonies.
pros: Historic 16th-century convent converted to luxury hotel
Prime location in Cusco's San Blas neighborhood near major attractions
Oxygen-enriched rooms to help with high altitude adjustment
Beautiful colonial architecture with modern luxury amenities
cons: High altitude location at 11,000+ feet above sea level
